newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Electrolux rally boosts Swedish shares to record.
newsitem.headline: Electrolux rally boosts Swedish shares to record.

text.p: The Stockholm Stock Exchange broke a day-old record to close at a high on Friday, helped by a rally in appliance maker Electrolux.
The Stockholm general index rose 0.62 percent to 2,915.32 in turnover totalling 6.2 billion crowns.
Electrolux touched a record at 600 but closed at 592, up 63, adding to a 64 crown gain made a day earlier after announcing a 2.5 billion crown restructruing programme.
Lehman Brothers set a mid-term price for Electrolux of 630 crowns and that it added Electrolux to its European strategy "recommended" list due to its restructuring plan.

"Considering the size of the company, not such a big change in the operating margins are needed to have large effects on the bottom line. So I think the share price reaction is motivated," said Henrik Breum at Aros Securities.
Ball bearing group SKF rose on speculation that the group would present a rationalisation programme in line with Electrolux's plans. The share rose 6.5 crowns to 186.5.

Drug company Pharmacia & Upjohn fell 6.5 crowns to 258, still hurt by rumours it would post a lower than expected second quarter profit. The group has, however, said that it had no plans to issue a profit warning.
"Even if P&U denied the rumours there is usually no smoke without fire," a trader said.
Telecoms group Ericsson rose one crown 299.5.
"Rumours that Ericsson was going to win a a big network order in the United States boosted the share in the afternoon. But there doesn't seem to be any substance to that," a broker said.
Clothing retailer Hennes & Maurtiz jumped 19.5 crowns to 267 ahead of its half-year result due on Monday on keen interest from international investors, brokers said.
